content:
maria: FYI we got reports from a few tenants that their v2 traffic silently fell back to v1 during yesterday's quota spike. Noticed in the SRE alerts and a couple support tickets.
jonas: Ooof. Any idea what triggered the fallbacks?
maria: Early signal points to the per-route rate cap we pushed as a hotfix. When the cap tripped the router seemed to prefer an old-version route instead of the configured fallback variant.
tara: Can we get logs? I want to check whether it was a deliberate feature of the router (route precedence) or a quirk in the header parity code.
kevin: Pasted the snippet from the edge logs:
```
[2025-04-11T18:02:12Z] token=abc123 route=projects/foo variant=v2 status=THROTTLED fallback_route=projects/foo/variant=v1 reason=RATE_CAP
[2025-04-11T18:02:12Z] routing_decision=sticky_match -> selected=projects/foo/variant=v1
```
kevin: Looks like the router marked the request as throttled and then did a sticky match to v1.
jonas: Sticky matching shouldn't override explicit fallback policy. That implies precedence is wrong when the throttle reason is RATE_CAP.
carol: From a console/UX perspective, tenants see no banner or metric indicating the fallback — they just observe degraded quality. We should surface a distinct telemetry metric and a per-route banner that says "Fallback to v1 due to capacity throttling" with counts.
tara: Agreed. Telemetry idea: emit event `route.fallback` with tags {route, selected_variant, reason, tenant_id}. That will let us filter by RATE_CAP vs other reasons.
maria: Also need a sampling plan so we don't blow metrics budgets. Maybe full counts every 5m + sampled traces for individual requests.
jonas: Implementation detail: router will need to attach a fallback_decision tag at time of selection, then pipeline to our metrics router. Can we add a small counter increment and an optional trace with the header set?
kevin: I can push a small change to mark precedence: when reason==RATE_CAP, prefer explicit `fallback_variant` over `sticky_match`. Quick PR would be to flip the branch and emit `route.fallback=rate_cap` counter.
carol: For the console: show a per-route skinny line item in the traffic table: "Fallbacks (rate cap)" with last-1h count and a link to sampled examples. Should be low-visibility by default but prominent in the incident view.
tara: Also: telemetry needs to tie back to billing and quota dashboards — otherwise teams won't correlate throttles to quota usage. Add `quota_window` and `quota_threshold` tags where possible.
maria: Action items: 1) kevin -> hotfix PR to router precedence and instrumentation (owner: kevin, ETA: today EOD). 2) jonas -> add metrics name and tag schema for `route.fallback` (ETA: tomorrow). 3) carol -> mockup console row & incident banner copy (ETA: tomorrow morning). 4) tara -> audit header parity code to ensure no silent suppression of the fallback tag (ETA: today).
kevin: Will create PR; will add unit that simulates throttle then sticky match.
jonas: Once PR is out we should run a purple-shadow test: force-ratecap on a shadow cohort and monitor `route.fallback` metric before enabling globally.
carol: UX note: banner copy should include recommended actions (increase reserved capacity, enable dedicated route, or accept fallback). Keep it short.
maria: Support desk: can we add a temporary query in Intercom to find tickets referencing "v2 -> v1" so CS can proactively reach out?
tara: I'll add a saved log query and notify CS.
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: kevin/router-precedence-fix -> canary in prod-1 at 2025-04-12T02:15:00Z.
maria: Thanks everyone. Let's sync if anything unexpected pops up during the canary.
carol: I'll share console mock in #design later today for quick review :thumbsup:
jonas: Marking this resolved for now pending canary metrics.
